[Professor Gary
Collins](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/staff/profiles/applied-health/collins-gary "Professor Gary Collins")
is a 125th Anniversary Chair and Professor of Medical Statistics at the
University of Birmingham, and a [NIHR Senior
Investigator](https://www.nihr.ac.uk/people/professor-gary-collins "NIHR Senior Investigator").
His primary research interests are primarily focussed on aspects
surrounding the development and validation multivariable prediction
models (design, analysis and reporting).

In 2010, he established an international initiative to develop the
[TRIPOD](https://doi.org/10.7326/M14-0697 "TRIPOD") reporting
recommendations published in 2015 for studies developing and validating
clinical prediction models. He led an update to these recommendations in
2024 to cover models developed using artificial intelligence and machine
learning methods
([TRIPOD+AI](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-078378 "TRIPOD+AI")) and
large language models
([TRIPOD-LLM](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03425-5 "TRIPOD-LLM")).

Gary has also been involved in other guidance for artificial
intelligence and machine learning studies in healthcare, including

- [STARD-AI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-025-03953-8 "STARD-AI") -
  for AI based diagnostic test accuracy studies
- [DECIDE-AI](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2022-070904 "DECIDE-AI") - for
  early-stage live clinical evaluation of AI systems
- [CONSORT-AI](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-1034-x "CONSORT-AI")
  / [SPIRIT-AI](https://www.bmj.com/content/370/bmj.m3210 "SPIRIT-AI") -
  for AI intervention studies
- [CHART](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjmed-2025-001632 "CHART") - for
  evaluating chatbots providing medical advice

Gary has also developed numerous other reporting guidelines for other study designs, including

- [GATHER](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(16)30388-9 "GATHER")
  statement for studies providing global health estimates
- [AGReMA](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2784353 "AGReMA")
  statement for mediation analyses
- 2025 update of
  [SPIRIT](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-081477 "SPIRIT") and
  [CONSORT](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-081123 "CONSORT")
  guidelines for clinical trials
- [SPIRIT-Surrogate](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-078525 "SPIRIT-Surrogate")
  and
  [CONSORT-Surrogate](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-078524 "CONSORT-Surrogate")
  for trials with surrogate endpoints

He has more than 500 peer-reviewed articles, editorials and
commentaries, including 90 in the ‘big 6′ medical journals.
